One of the things that there are, guidelines in how attorneys often interpret code, sometimes they'll look to see if the language is specific as opposed to general, if it's exclusive as opposed to inclusive. But my point is that the code is very specifically specifies that for a single family home in the R1 an underground garage is not permitted, not permissible. Our code also has a lot, there's a lot of language regarding whether the square footage of a garage should count to FAR. And presumably at some point it wasn't counted towards FAR. And what that meant was that people built their homes to the maximum of the FAR and they were encouraged to have two or three car garages, which increased the entire size of the home. It just says very clearly that below grade single family improvements don't count towards the total FAR. I think where the nuance here is, is this notion that what applies to a single family home in an R1 necessarily applies to a non single family home in an R1. And this is actually what's so complicated about our zoning, which is that we don't zone a parcel for a school. And so we create a, I'm not disagreeing with you. One time I heard council discuss underground garages and someone suggested that maybe one of the reasons why they stopped allowing them in the mid nineties was because when people back out of underground garage, back out of underground garages, it creates a danger for people walking on the sidewalk. That limitation doesn't specifically apply to non-single family homes in R1. And that's the crux of the situation. So consequently, while the discussion in some of this correspondence regarding the term substantial hardship, which you'll find in our ordinance in subpart A may be intellectually interesting, it's not controlling because hardship is not a required element of any of the four findings we have to make.
